title: Introduce throughput continuity controller and deferred warmup credit gauge
author: Diego Ramirez
release_notes: Introduces a new throughput continuity controller to smooth throughput during capacity changes and a deferred warmup credit gauge to prevent premature burst allocation. Includes metrics, docs, and tests. Backwards-compatible runtime additions.
description: Context: We have recurring throughput blips when Dedicated pools scale down/up or when warm pools are still ramping. These transient gaps cause consumer errors and tail-latency spikes even though overall capacity is sufficient. This PR implements a continuity controller that maintains short-term throughput guarantees across transient capacity transitions, plus a deferred warmup credit gauge that prevents the autoscaler from allocating burst credits until warmlets report readiness. Motivation: reduce 95p/99p latency regressions during scale events and avoid overcommitting burst tokens to tenants when warm pools aren't warmed yet. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-4721) - [x] Continuity controller implementation - [x] Deferred warmup credit gauge + metrics - [x] Unit tests for controller logic and gauge edge cases - [x] Integration test simulating pool resize and warmlet lag - [x] Console docs for Dedicated tuning - [x] Backfill changelog entry Summary of changes (commits): * Add continuity controller core loop and state machine (continuity_controller.go) * Add deferred warmup gauge and metrics exporter (warmup_gauge.go) * Integrate controller into provisioner pipeline and admission path (provisioner_integration.go) * Add unit + e2e tests and flakey-case harness adjustments (continuity_controller_test.go, e2e/warmup_resize_sim.go) * Update docs and helm values for default thresholds (console/docs/dedicated/autoscaling.md, deploy/k8s/helm/values.yaml) Changed areas (high-level): - serving/autoscaler/continuity_controller.go: new controller that tracks recent capacity delta events, computes continuity budgets (ms tokens) per pool, and issues short-lived soft-reservations to smooth throughput without violating long-term reservations. - serving/autoscaler/continuity_controller_test.go: deterministic unit tests for the continuity state machine and backpressure behavior. - serving/metrics/warmup_gauge.go: new metric that reports warmup-ready-credit and a deferred_ready boolean per pool; exposes Prometheus metrics and console summary. - provisioner/provisioner_integration.go: hooks to consider continuity budgets and deferred warmup state during admission and burst allocation. - console/docs/dedicated/autoscaling.md: guidance, default thresholds, and examples for tuning continuity and warmup gating. - deploy/k8s/helm/values.yaml: new config options under dedicated.autoscaling.continuity and warmup.gauge thresholds. - e2e/warmup_resize_sim.go: deterministic sim that reproduces previous flakiness and verifies continuity smoothing reduces tail latency. Review conversation (excerpted as a single continuous transcript): Reviewer Ayesha Patel: "This is promising — main question is how we bound budget growth when multiple pools experience simultaneous small deltas. Without a cap we could temporarily allocate too much soft-reservation capacity." Author reply (Diego): "Good point. I added a per-pool cap (configurable) and a global budget ceiling; see continuity_controller.go lines ~120-160. The controller decays unused budget exponentially with configurable half-life so growth is controlled." Reviewer Ben Cho: "Observed a race in drain path where continuity soft reservations were not released if a node drain preempted the warmlet readiness callback — leads to sticky reserved slots." Author: "Fixed: added a finalizer hook invoked on drain events to force-release continuity reservations; added a test (continuity_controller_test.go::TestDrainRelease)." Reviewer Lucas Meyer: "CI showed a flaky test (AutoscalerSuite/TestWarmupDrain) on first run; please add retry or make deterministic." Author: "Converted the test harness to deterministic timing using injected clock and removed time.Sleep; rerun CI (flaky passed on rerun)." Maintainer Samir Gupta: "LGTM after fixes — approved to squash-merge once CI green." CI summary: - initial run: build + unit tests + integration -> one flaky: AutoscalerSuite/TestWarmupDrain failed on timing assertion - rerun: CI passed all checks; metrics exporter lint and docs build succeeded Observability and metrics: - new Prometheus metrics: redwood_autoscaler_continuity_budget_ms{pool,region}, redwood_autoscaler_warmup_deferred_ready{pool}=0/1, redwood_autoscaler_warmup_credit_total - dashboards: Dedicated > Autoscaling > Continuity (new) with budget burn-down and per-pool deferred-ready heatmap Tuning defaults (reasoned choices): - continuity.max_budget_ms: 30000 (protects against unbounded smoothing) - continuity.decay_half_life_s: 60 - warmup.defer_until_ready: true - warmup.min_ready_fraction: 0.67 Testing notes: - unit tests cover the state transitions, cap behavior, and decay math using a fake clock - e2e sim reproduces a 3x warmlet lag scenario and asserts 99p latency drop of >= 12% with controller enabled Migration/backwards compatibility: - All changes are additive; existing reservation semantics unchanged. New config keys are optional with safe defaults. No migration scripts required. Rollout plan: - Canary the continuity controller in a single Dedicated region with conservative defaults (max_budget_ms=15000) - Observe Budget burn and warmup_deferred_ready signals; expose alert if continuity_budget_ms > 75% for > 5m - After 48h, increase canary scope if no regressions Metrics/telemetry cost impact: minimal — two new counters/gauges per pool. Docs: - console/docs/dedicated/autoscaling.md contains user-facing tuning guidance and impact on tenant burst behavior. Merge outcome: Squash-merged by Samir Gupta after addressing reviewer feedback and CI re-run. Backports: None (non-breaking). Related: ENG-4721, PM-891, SUP-342.
